translation_notes: graph.objects(tm, uri(_R2RML + "predicateObjectMap")) then graph.objects(pom, uri(_R2RML + "objectMap")) is a genuine two-step chain (every pom must have come from tm, every om from pom -- not independently optional siblings), so it becomes one joined `for pom, om in m{ {tm} r2rml:predicateObjectMap ?pom . ?pom r2rml:objectMap ?om }`, matching the nested-loop cross product exactly.

the remaining graph.objects(om, uri(X)) calls use predicates that are only known at run time (drawn from tuples like _TERM_TYPE_PREDS, _REFERENCE_PREDS, _FUNCTION_EXECUTION_PREDS mixing rml/fnml-old/r2rml variants), so they stay individual m{ {om} {uri(pred)} ?v } with the predicate interpolated -- m{ } takes a written pattern, not a dynamic list of alternative predicates, so the Python-level `for pred in PREDS:` loop around it could not be folded in.

context shim (rml_context.py) reconstructs _local_name and the recursive _fn_source_columns helper (and the _RMLF/_FNML_OLD/_INPUT_PREDS/_INPUT_VALUE_MAP_PREDS constants they need) verbatim from the upstream source at the pinned commit; _REFERENCE_PREDS/_FUNCTION_EXECUTION_PREDS/_R2RML/_TERM_TYPE_PREDS are the region's own module-level constants and stay in original.py/translated.ldpy.

classified minor-restructuring rather than directly-expressible only because of the predicate-interpolation workaround needed for the dynamic term-type/reference/function predicates -- the traversal shape itself (the join) is a direct fit.

repair.driver: 6 calls added to the existing one: the inline graph plus a second triples map tm2 (own reference and one-column function), called on tm and on tm2; fixture_mapping.ttl, a mapping in the repository's real shape (IRI triples maps, blank-node predicate-object and object maps, legacy rml#/fnml# namespaces, w3id rml:termType rml:IRI, a predicate-object map with two object maps, neighbours through rr:predicateMap, the subject map and a predicate other than rr:predicateObjectMap), called on two maps, on a map without predicate-object map and on an IRI that is no subject (zero solutions).
mutants_killed: {om} -> ?_o in each of the three inner islands

optimization_notes: optimized.py: `import rdflib` plus `uri = rdflib.URIRef` become `from rdflib import URIRef as uri`; is_iri is inlined in its `if any(...)`; the reference loop becomes `out.update(<generator>)`. The function-execution loop stays (its len(cols) test needs cols twice, and a walrus is not allowed). The result is a set, so only its content counts.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: the two outer loops become one join under `@graph graph`, `m{ {tm} r2rml:predicateObjectMap _:pom . _:pom r2rml:objectMap ?om }`. pom is not used in the body, so a labelled blank node joins without being projected; the matcher reads the patterns in the order written, so the traversal starts from tm as the nested loops do. The bracket form `[ r2rml:objectMap ?om ]` is one token shorter but transpiles inner triple first, which scans every rr:objectMap triple in the graph on each call; it is not used. The three reads over a predicate from a run-time tuple become `m{ {om} {uri(p)} ?v }` (predicate interpolated), each one token shorter than `graph.objects(om, uri(p))` (measured).

Exception to the symmetry: merging the pom/om loops is a restructuring only the multi-pattern m{ } allows (in Python, a generator over the two selectors is longer than the nested loops). The labelled blank node used as an unprojected join variable has no label in the closed construction vocabulary; it is counted under m{ }.
header_optimization_notes: Nothing unused on either side: the shim import and the five constants are all read (by the region or by the tuples it reads), and the r2rml: prefix is used. optimized_header.py and optimized_header.ldpy are copies of the optimized artefacts.
